title: The Complete Guide to Packshot Photography, 2: Photo Equipment and What You Need to Know

description: In this 2nd article of our packshot photography guide, find out what photo equipment you need to create good packshots!
author: PackshotCreator
content:
Welcome to the second installment of our comprehensive guide to packshot photography. In this article, we'll cover the essential aspects of photo equipment suited to packshot photography, as well as the basics you need to know to get the best results.

Whether you are a company looking to maximize the online sales of its products, a professional just starting out, or an experienced photographer looking to improve your skills in this field, this comprehensive guide will give you a wealth of practical and technical information for successful product photography. Proven advice, helpful tips, and cutting-edge techniques will help you get the most out of your photo equipment and produce professional-quality images.

So make yourself comfortable, grab your camera, and get ready to discover the secrets of packshot photography.

Camera equipment: What do you need to take packshot photographs of your products?

Make sure you have enough space in your premises in advance

First of all, make sure you have enough space to take your packshot photographs: photo equipment quickly takes up room! The space you'll need depends largely on the method you choose for taking your packshots:

‍

‍

  • If you want to set up a traditional photo studio on your premises, you will need enough space for all your lights, a platform for your products, the background, the rest of your photo equipment, etc.
  • If you opt instead for an automated photo studio like the ones we sell, note that they come in a much more compact format than a traditional photo studio.

Whichever you choose, you'll also need enough space next to your studio to gather your products before shooting them, as well as a surface to open, prepare and clean them if necessary, and then repack them.

Choose your camera equipment carefully and in particular the camera

For successful product packshot photography, it is crucial to choose the right photo equipment, especially your camera. In the skincare and cosmetics industry, a camera with excellent color reproduction is essential to accurately represent product hues. It can make a huge difference in image quality and visual impact.

But what type of camera should you choose? Cameras come in a wide range of types and prices.

It might be tempting to stick with smartphones, but their image quality is too limited for good packshot photography.

‍

‍

Instead, we recommend investing in a dedicated camera. DSLR cameras are widely considered to be the de facto standard for product packshot photography: they offer high-resolution images and great versatility.
But what really matters is the sensor size and quality of your camera, which has a significant influence on the resolution and level of detail of your photos.
The most common sensor sizes are full frame (35mm wide) and APS-C (24mm wide). For packshot photography, we recommend opting for APS-C, which offers a greater depth of field and therefore a sharper product in the frame.
In addition to choosing the right camera, you'll also need to think about the rest of your photo equipment, such as lenses and tripods. In the high-tech, household appliances and computer sector, macro lenses may be required to capture small components accurately. Lenses are important for getting the right focal length, aperture and sharpness, while tripods help keep the camera stable and minimize blur caused by camera movement.

Take care of your lighting

To take quality packshot photographs, lighting is a crucial element that should not be overlooked: good lighting will allow you to highlight your products' features, texture and details, and thus make them attractive to your customers.
First of all, you should know that the ideal lighting for product photography is soft, even light, without unwanted shadows or reflections. Be aware, though, that this does not mean you should leave no shadows at all in the final shot: a product without a shadow is also a product without depth. However, care must be taken not to add unnecessary shadows.
To achieve this, several solutions and pieces of photo equipment are available: use a softbox (a diffused light box), place reflective or diffusing panels around your product, or place lights on either side of it, preferably using LED bulbs.

‍

‍

It is also important to take into account the color temperature of the lighting you use. The color temperature of light can influence how your products are perceived. For example, light that is too cool may give an impression of sterility, while light that is too warm may alter the colors of your product. It is therefore recommended to use neutral white light, with a color temperature of 5500K.

Another photo equipment tip: we also recommend working with a tripod to avoid blur, especially if you use a slow shutter speed to let in more light.

Opt for a suitable background

In packshot photography, always use the simplest possible background. The goal is not to distract attention from the product.

‍

‍
An overly busy or colorful background may distract the customer's eye and detract from the presentation of your product. Likewise, a gray or black background can “crush” the product.
So keep it as simple as possible and opt for a perfectly white, plain background. This will also make it even easier to cut out the product later to obtain a transparent background for other media!

Ensure the repeatability of your shots

When taking packshot photographs to showcase your products online, it is essential to pay particular attention to the repeatability and homogeneity of your shots. For all of your products to be presented consistently, you need to reproduce a similar shooting setup for each of them.

‍

‍

However, maintaining this consistency can be a daunting task when working with a traditional photo studio and all the photo equipment that goes with it. The logistics of setting up each product can quickly become cumbersome and make it difficult to achieve an acceptable level of uniformity.

That is why we strongly recommend that you draw up a precise setup plan for your photo equipment, carefully measuring the distances and angles and recording the various settings used, to ensure that each shot is the same as the previous one. This rigor will save you from having to retouch each photo individually in post-production, even though it will inevitably take some preparation time.

Note that if you use one of our automated studios, you can save all your positions and settings and reuse them in one click from one photo to the next, making this step totally trivial! You'll also have much less photo equipment to take out and put back each time.

Use good post-production software

Powerful post-production software not only makes it possible to remove any imperfections that could affect image quality, but above all lets you adjust brightness and sharpness, crop, or even remove the background: all essential steps to obtain a perfect packshot.

With this in mind, Adobe Photoshop is a great example of post-production software for editing packshot photographs. After all, this software is renowned for its ability to process high-quality images with great precision and flexibility.

However, using this type of photo software is not something you can improvise. Mastering Photoshop's features takes time and practice. Learning to handle the various image processing options requires a certain amount of expertise that only an experienced user can acquire.

It is therefore essential to factor in the time needed to learn this type of post-production software. You need to be ready to invest time and money in training your employees to obtain high-quality packshots.

How can an automated in-house photo studio be interesting for your business?

Investing in an in-house automated photo studio can be extremely beneficial for businesses, for several key reasons.

Homogeneity and standardization

First of all, it is essential to fully understand the concept of flow: throughout the year, product shoots follow one another according to the calendar, stock arrivals, marketing needs and so on. However, all photos must remain consistent and uniform to reflect a professional brand image.

‍

‍

And as we explained above, meeting this requirement takes a lot of effort when you use a traditional photo studio and all the photo equipment that comes with it, whereas an automated photo studio is designed to considerably simplify this flow and keep it consistent.

Thanks to specialized photo equipment fully controlled by intuitive, easy-to-use software, you can easily achieve consistent, uniform photo quality no matter the time of year. Save all your settings and positions in a few clicks so you can quickly reuse them for all your shots!

A complete and turnkey solution

‍

‍

In addition, an automated photo studio combines all your photo equipment into a single system: lighting, background, product positioning, 360-degree views and post-production. This not only saves a lot of time and manual work, but also reduces the errors and costs associated with photography. You can thus increase your productivity while ensuring superior photo quality.

Access to multiple media

An automated photo studio also allows you to work with various types of media. In addition to traditional still photos, it is often possible to create 360-degree views, videos and animations to highlight your products.

‍

‍

Investing in an in-house automated photo studio can therefore offer you numerous advantages. In addition to saving time and money, an automated photo studio allows you to produce professional, consistent and uniform photos, while offering the opportunity to explore other types of media. We will discuss this in more detail in the following articles in this series.

How to take packshot photographs: the basics you need to know

If your business wants to get started in packshot photography, it is imperative to follow some basic rules to get professional results.

The presentation

First of all, presentation must be meticulous: it is important to take the time to arrange the product properly, to place it at an angle that favors the light and to think about its position in the frame.

It is also crucial to clean and prepare the product before photographing it. Stains or scratches on the object would have a negative impact on the final image. It may seem obvious, but it can make a big difference when shooting.

The background

Once again, the choice of background is an important aspect of packshot photography. Ideally, use a neutral white background, as it will enhance the product and maintain visual balance. Colored backgrounds can distract attention and compromise image quality. Remember: we have no artistic pretensions here; the primary objective is to present the product faithfully.

The sharpness

‍

‍

Finally, it is crucial to avoid blur anywhere on the product by using the technique known as “focus stacking”. This technique consists of taking several photos, changing the focus point for each shot, and then combining them to obtain an image that is sharp across the entire object. This way, the product is truly represented as it is, and full sharpness is maintained. While focus stacking is quite time-consuming with a traditional photo studio, it can be done automatically with an automated photo studio.

The details

To produce quality packshot photographs, you must therefore take care of every detail, use the right shooting techniques, and use the appropriate retouching tools. This is also where you can see how an automated photo studio can make it easier for you to take packshots at every stage.

There are still many other elements to consider in order to take good packshot photographs that really showcase your products, and we will cover them in the following articles:

  • How to adapt your photographs and settings according to the type of product and its specificities.
  • What type of media to choose according to your product.
  • What is the best way to ensure consistency between each of your photos for a highly professional result.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a classic product photo and a packshot?
faqs.answer: A classic product photo can include decorative elements, staging, or context of use. A packshot, on the other hand, is more technical and standardized: the product is generally isolated on a neutral background, photographed from several angles, with optimal lighting that reveals all the details and characteristics of the product. The packshot favors precision and clarity over the artistic aspect.

faqs.question: What is the difference between packshot, lifestyle and still life?
faqs.answer: A packshot focuses on faithfully representing the product on a neutral background for e-commerce. Lifestyle photography shows the product in its context of use, while still life takes an artistic approach to brand communication.

faqs.question: Why avoid generic supplier photos?
faqs.answer: Using the same photos as your competitors undermines your differentiation. An automated photo studio makes it possible to create unique visuals that reinforce your brand identity and increase the trust of customers, who see exactly what they are buying.

faqs.question: How many photos do you usually need for a complete packshot?
faqs.answer: A complete packshot typically includes a main front view showing the product from the front, two to three views from different angles to show volume and shape, a rear view to show packaging information, and one to two detail views to highlight important product features. You can also add a 360-degree view made up of 24 to 72 images, depending on the precision you want. For e-commerce, a minimum of 5 to 7 photos is generally recommended to give a complete view of the product and reduce buyer uncertainty.

faqs.question: What lenses are recommended for packshot photography?
faqs.answer: Several types of lenses are useful depending on the products to be photographed. A macro lens in the 85mm-105mm range is ideal for capturing small products and details with exceptional precision. For great versatility, a standard 50mm prime lens with a good aperture (f/1.8 or f/1.4) is an excellent choice for most common products. If you're working with products of varying sizes, a professional-quality zoom lens such as a 24-70mm offers the flexibility to adapt quickly to different situations. In all cases, priority should be given to lenses that provide excellent sharpness and minimize distortion in order to accurately represent the products.
